reviewScope: One combined initial review of both complete source tasks; actual three original PNGs inspected via view_image, with editable native tables and diagram code examined. No rendering performed.

The source image has one-unit subdivisions; both native graphs omit these and leave only five-unit grid lines. This removes meaningful plotting precision for 36, 12 and 6. Marks omitted as instructed.

reviews.teachingFit: Fits inverse-variation model building on p6 and ordinary substitution, table and graph transfer. The belief is preserved as a hypothesis, not asserted as physical fact.
requiredEdits: Restore the original one-unit grid subdivisions on the editable question graph so that the requested points can be plotted accurately; restore them on the solution graph as well for consistent reading of those points. Retain the five-unit and ten-unit hierarchy, labels, blank question grid and existing curve.
reviews.difficultyReason: A routine linked sequence: set up an inverse model from a pair, calculate the constant, substitute into a scaffolded table and translate the results to a curve on supplied axes. The multipart form is not itself the source of demand.

reviews.sourceNativeFidelity: All five parts, formulae, context, units and source ordering retained, with native a–e labels and marks removed. The editable graph retains the original axes, units, major ticks and one-fifth subdivisions and labels the theoretical and actual cubic curves; the computed curves match the given model. Final-size rendering was outside this review.
reviews.answersVerified: 7.3³×20000=7,780,340 W; 0.4×20000w³=8000w³; at 9 m/s the difference is 14,580,000−5,832,000=8,748,000 W, with reasonable graph approximations accepted. For 4.4 million W, w³=550 and w≈8.1932 m/s, consistent with the source graph-read approximation 8.2 m/s. For fixed r, a 10% wind increase multiplies power by 1.1³=1.331, hence a 33.1% increase; the numerical worked values also check. Both Short and Worked are correct.
reviews.teachingFit: P16 establishes power variation and comparison after changing an input; p6 supports model relationships. Formula substitution, percentage multipliers and interpreting the supplied graph are ordinary component transfers; no identical worked example is required.
reviews.difficultyReason: Several scaffolded linked calculations culminate in comparing a 10% input increase with the cubic output change. This requires coordinating a percentage multiplier and power model but the formula and context are supplied; the number of parts does not inflate the score.
